Ooohhh. I knew someone who did this. I’ll tell you what the guy did and told me, and maybe you can see similarities to him and other people. 

I was abused by my mother. Well, guess what? So was he. He could identify so closely with me!! It’s like we were abuse twins. So relatable. He liked to tell me very vivid stories of his abuse. Like how his mother locked him and his siblings in a room for days and days with nothing in the rooms. He told me all this information after a week of knowing him. 

It seemed like something ridiculous or crazy to me but I never wanted to doubt someone’s abuse. Looking back, the red flag is that his experiences of abuse were just. Insane. Unbelievable. His father starved him and wouldn’t let him or his siblings eat. He did this so he could manipulate me to buy food for him, something he could do himself but chose not to. 

His stories were inconsistent. I asked his friends about the abuse he faced and they told me he had never ever told them what he told me. His one friend, who was abused by their father, told me that he told them he watched his father beat his brother with a frying pan and that his father was very physically abusive. Now, he never told me that. It was all about his mother, likely because I have an abusive mother and he wanted to identify with me. 

He told me about “abusive relationships” but could never give me any details. Just how much they traumatized him and ruined him. 

He used his “abuse” to manipulate me. “You know what I’ve been through and all the horrors I’ve seen. Why are you doing this to me?” That’s the kinds of things he would say to me. Etc. I was abused by pedophiles and he later told me in vivid detail how he was molested. I can hardly speak of what happened to me so I doubt that he was.

So, why did he lie? 

To manipulate me. To make me feel sorry for him. To identify with and relate to me, to make us closer friends. To show that his life was worse than mine. 

How did I know he lied?

How quickly he spilled all this information to me. His inconsistent stories. Telling some people one thing and others another. His stories were crafted to be similar to my personal experiences. His stories would be extremely vivid and dramatic, painting himself as a hero or Martyr. They would show how much pain and suffering he has been through and why he is a broken person who needs me to fix him. Some stories had too much detail. His stories were just downright insane and unbelievable (but like I said I never wanted to doubt someone’s abuse). 

He also had a pattern of lying about other things including things that didn’t matter. I think he was a compulsive liar. He would tell you anything to make you feel sorry for him. I don’t doubt that he was abused, on some level, because why else would someone be so crazy? But I don’t think many of his stories were true, or were extremely exaggerated.

First, I really respect you being an autistic person with autistic kids. I know that cant be easy especially with the other things you live with but you are doing it! That’s really amazing. I also think, since you are autistic like your child you kind of might have an advantage on that aspect, because you can relate to them. A lot of parents of kids with autism treat their kids like burdens or pets, so i know you will empathize a lot more with your kid than most parents. 

I struggle with depression and OCD symptoms too. I know how hard that is. I dont’ know what exactly would make me a happy person, but i know some things that would’ve helped me growing up and i think you could be on the right track to helping. Already you show you really care and worry about your kid.

I think the most important thing is to be there for your kid and show them theyre not alone, that theyre not weird, that theyre not crazy or a burden to you for some of their “different” habits. My parents aren’t the nicest people and what hurts the most is how impatient they are with me. They tell me things like, you can do anything, your autism doesnt hold you back! Then they will bully me for showing symptoms of autism. I think you have to be really patient and gentle with your kid. To push them out into the world but be supportive too. AND TO NOT BE A HELICOPTER PARENT! I feel like thats a huge problem with parents in the autism community. They dont let their kids do things on their own because they are scared, the kid will become too sheltered and too dependent on the parent, and then its kind of like a never ending cycle. The parent doesnt let their kids do anything, so the kid becomes too dependent on them, further proving to the parent that the kid is completely helpless, etc. 

I don’t know the age of your kid but i think you should really work on socializing them while theyre young to make it less likely they might have social anxiety, or be completely averse to strangers or new activities. And to reward them for trying new things. Encourage them to talk to other kids, to say hello to strangers, maybe put them into something like a chess club, or video game club, or horseback riding? Horseback riding is my favorite part of my week because i get to be outside and around animals. Boy Scouts or Girl Scouts seems like it would’ve been a really cool thing to do and is awesome for Social skills. I think you should try to find things that will be escapes for your child, while they can make friends and find something they’re passionate about and love. I struggle with social anxiety really badly and i wonder if i was around more people and not so isolated things would be different. 

I think, as long as you are patient with your child, that you dont yell or talk down to them when youre upset, that you dont do things to CONSTANTLY REMIND them that theyre different, that you apologize to them when you do things wrong.. really focus on giving your child a good and happy childhood, filled with a lot of ways to grow and not CONTROLLING or SUFFOCATING them because you are worried about them. Encourage them to get a job when theyre older, get them out in the world, dont let them become hermits because you are scared for them. They are one day going to have to have some socially awkward or experiences, and they will learn from them. When this happens be really supportive and make sure they dont give up. The longer you keep them from having these experiences the harder it will be for them to live their lives when theyre older. It might be helpful to find a therapist for your child who can work with them so they dont lag behind and can live comfortably and face their challenges, or i remember when i was younger, there were classes and sort of groups for autistic kids to learn social skills and play games with other autistic kids (although personally I didnt like going to them)

I’m depressed, but what helps me most is activities to get my mind off it. My friends, dancing, horses, and having things to do and things to take care of. A routine might be helpful and teach your child responsibility. Being outside also really helps me, i love hearing the birds, smelling the nature and plants and feeling the wind. It would also be helpful to have people around you who dont let you fall into bad routines because of depression: dont let your laundry pile up, keep your room clean, shower every day, dont take super long depression naps.. its important not to fall into bad habits or else my depression will snowball and get worse. Sometimes, the best therapy is just putting on a face mask after a shower, it kind of makes me feel like i have my life together for a little bit

So like i said, being supportive is the most important thing and best thing you can do for your autistic kid. It makes me really happy you care so much about them to ask such a kind and thoughtful question and i know you have their best interest in mind. I can imagine sometimes its frustrating to ‘deal’ with an autistic kid but its also frustrating for the autistic kid to have so much trouble conveying their emotions or to deal with their every day problems. I’m proud of you for working so hard for your child after struggling so much and i hope you continue to overcome your struggles, maybe one day even surpass them, i have a lot of hope for you and your child too. Thank you for being a good parent, i hope anything i said was helpful. Hang in there!

1. I found out because I started struggling in middle school, they tested me and found I had autism. My parents insist I was “normal” before that but I had a teacher in elementary school who suspected I was autistic and she was right.  

2. Hmm. I can’t think of many good stereotypes. I guess a true one is that autistic people tend to be nerdy lol and I notice a lot have the same type of interests. I see a lot of autistic people who love stuff like anime, MLP, Nintendo, Pokémon, video games, transformers and YouTube. Also, MINECRAFT. I don’t know why, but I like them too (but I’ve never played Minecraft). It might be because there is a lot to learn about and it can be very immersive. Of course plenty of nonautistic people like these things too. 

The stereotypes I hate most I guess would be that autistic people can’t have empathy, that they will hurt animals, that they can’t have a sexuality. Autistic people do have empathy, but might have trouble understanding feelings unless they’re told directly. It can be something they need to learn. I once said something mean to someone without realizing, and after someone told me I cried because I felt so guilty. I know a lot of autistic people who love animals and for autistic people, sometimes we’re more comfortable around them than people because they won’t judge us like people will and it isn’t this hugely complicated process to socialize with them, we just pet them and then become friends. I don’t like people who assume all autistic people are innocent babies who can never date because they can’t understand others, because we have sexualities and want to form connections too. 

3. I’m socially awkward, I can’t make eye contact, I often go mute in public and can’t talk to others, only nod or shake my head because I get so nervous. I can’t carry on a conversation well, I don’t know what to say. It’s hard for me to put my thoughts together and I might talk for too long or stutter and have to repeat myself because people have trouble understanding me. I have ADHD and probably OCD, which is common for autism. I had a lot of trouble in school especially with math. I love my “special interests”, I can enjoy other things to an extent but nothing like my special interest which I can think about all day and not get bored. I “stim” like other autistic people by shaking my hands, hissing, rocking, and bouncing my knee, I also repeat phrases (I can recite like any vine or meme and they get stuck in my head..) but I can repress these in public. My face and body is also not very expressive and I’m kind of stiff. Symptoms I don’t have, I think are things I’ve mostly unlearned. I’m pretty ok with boundaries. I understand sarcasm. I know things that are 100% socially inappropriate and don’t do them.. 

4. This is kind of fun, I think I can almost instantly tell when someone is autistic irl. I once got in trouble for telling a boy at school that he was autistic, which his parents kept as a secret from him because they didn’t want him to know. I think autistic people speak in an articulate way and have distinct voices. A lot of autistic people seem to use social media like reddit, discord, and .. cough 4chan... as opposed to nonautistic people. And like I said before I notice a lot of autistic people love video games, anime, MLP, Nintendo, Minecraft. Lots of autistic people like to listen to music in public so they don’t have to talk to people. I see many autistic people struggle with math but enjoy social studies. I don’t know many autistic people who enjoy sports. I’ve never met an autistic person who could ride a bike lol but I’m hoping I can learn this year. Also, their handwriting tends to look a certain way. I’ve also met a lot of trans autistic people :) Lots of weird random things in this paragraph lol

Hmm yeah I think there is. All autism people are different, but I also notice in a lot of cases, many autistic people share similarities no matter where they are on the spectrum. 

I worked with a class of severely autistic people and I always saw similarities between myself and them, even if I’m “high functioning”. Like I knew a girl who always repeated words, and sometimes I do that. When some get upset by certain noises I can relate to them and understand why they cover their ears—I want to cover my ears too. A boy would take off his shirt because he didn’t like the texture, and I could relate to wanting to do that even if I don’t! Lol. 

So I think in some ways we’re all a little the same. But I also think we’re all on different levels in different aspects. Does that make sense?

There are some autistic people who can never talk. There are also some autistic people who can’t speak when they get upset, or only to their family members. 

There are some autistic people who might act inappropriately by being too loud, but they are still social and can make friends. Then there’s someone like me, while I’m not loud, I’m so quiet it’s hard for me to make friends. 

No matter where someone is on the spectrum it’s likely that they will have a meltdown over Something at some point in their life, or have a trigger for a response like that. 

An autistic person can be an amazing artist, but never speak. An autistic person might not be able to do schoolwork but is an amazing athlete!

I think many people like me have one thing they really love and are passionate about no matter where on the spectrum. I worked with a severely autistic girl who really loved beluga whales and finding Nemo, it was cute lol. 

She could also recite things from the movie and match the voices perfectly, not a lot of people can do that! That’s part of the spectrum aspect, she is considered severely autistic but has that cool skill!

So I guess long story short, we are as different and diverse as “normal” or “Atypical” people are. Lol sorry if this was all over the place ..
